evidence_type: Assistant in-memory transcription of the learner-supplied DBeaver result screenshot; no direct database read.
query_type: Single read-only twelve-week price-context query; no table created or updated.
selection_policy: Same accepted highest-90-day-unit A x Z product, item_id ascending tie-break; no hard-coded source identifier.
price_policy: Same-store prices are compared only with the immediately preceding displayed week when both records exist. First-week comparable/up/down counts are NULL. Missing zero-sales store/week prices remain unknown and are not zero-filled or bridged; missing prices with positive recorded units fail. Min/max use observed prices only.
display_normalization: Unit totals and store comparison counts are canonical JSON integers or null. Displayed price extrema are numeric strings padded to two decimals. Week dates use YYYY-MM-DD; first-week comparable/up/down values are JSON null, not zero. Product identifiers, dates and PASS statuses are preserved only inside the in-memory canonical twelve-column rows before hashing.
fingerprint_method: SHA256 of UTF-8 compact JSON with sorted object keys and ensure_ascii=False. Report rows are chronological; units and counts are JSON integers, price extrema two-decimal strings or NULL, and first-week comparison counts NULL. Identifiers occur only in memory before hashing.
scope: All twelve screenshot rows and twelve displayed fields were transcribed only in memory. The ordered canonical price-report SHA-256 fingerprint exactly matches the historical assistant preflight and independent reference. All displayed dates, units, price extrema, coverage counts, first-week NULLs, comparison counts and PASS statuses are included. Public acceptance retains only aggregate controls and a fingerprint, without the real selected identifier, weekly rows, store prices, numeric vectors or screenshot. The observed 110 transitions represent ten stores across eleven adjacent displayed-week pairs, not 110 stores. This confirms learner execution and displayed output, not a direct audit of underlying store prices, original CSVs or every grid position. Independent source reconstruction, the selected 840 daily records and 120 source prices, baseline fields, thirty-six targeted cases, source/input fingerprints and timings remain separate assistant evidence. The first-week comparison NULLs are preserved and not interpreted as no price change. Interpretation is attributed to the assistant; simultaneous price and sales movements do not establish promotion, price elasticity, causal response, availability or stockout. The next planned checkpoint consolidates accepted business findings and prepares forecasting scope; no forecasting model, baseline evaluation or final-holdout result is claimed.
